description: A single-expression arm body ends at its line break: the `"orphan"` line after `.A :> return` is not part of the arm, and a line at arm level that is no arm is a parse error (E-PARSE-001), not a silently dropped statement and not `return "orphan"`. (impl#1-legacy dialect — see rationale.)
rationale: IMPL#1-LEGACY behaviour (S469, dpa-073 F5): this case pins impl#1's newline-terminated reading, which impl#1 keeps as a carried divergence — it is NOT the language rule. Under SPEC §7.2.2 as rewritten S469 (dpa-073 F1 (a)) a line break is whitespace, a leave operand ends at the arm's `,` or the list's `}` (§18.2 "Extent"), and arms are a comma list; this source (no arm commas, no `;`) is not ruled-dialect input. Pre-S469 rationale, kept for the record: §7.2.2 (S446) rule 8 "`return` ends at the line break" and "Arm heads" made the `"orphan"` line a parse error; impl#1 had joined the lines into `return return "orphan"` (dpa-068 D8).
